cues.en: Every letter to get where it's going requires the address, obviously, but also a mysterious string of characters called a postcode. But if there's an address already, what's the point of the postcode exactly? Isn't this just like the address again? Kind of yes, but also no, because there's two answers to why this if also that. For the first, while every country has their own postcode particulars, to start simple, we're going to start with the states who sticks with just simple digits. But does it a bit different by being the only one on earth to call their code a zip code along with The Philippines. But anyway, the usual way to describe how this five digit code works is by starting with the first digits to divide America into 10 zones. Beginning with New England as zero and... Oh, New Jersey too? Really America? There's a non contiguous exception before we've even counted to one. So New England ish, I guess? Oh, but also Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands only 7%
cues.zh: 显然，信件要送到目的地需要地址，但还需要一串神秘的字符，也就是邮政编码。但既然已经有了地址，邮政编码到底有什么用呢？这不就跟地址重复了吗？某种程度上算是，但也不完全是，因为关于“为什么既有这个又有那个”，有两个答案。首先，虽然每个国家都有自己的邮编特色，但为了简单起见，我们先从只使用简单数字的美国开始。不过美国有点不同，它是世界上仅有的两个把邮编叫作 zip code 的国家之一，另一个是菲律宾。不管怎样，通常解释这五位数字编码工作原理的方法，是从第一位数字开始的，它把美国划分为10个区域。以新英格兰为0开始，还有……哦，还有新泽西？真的吗，美国？我们还没数到1呢，就出现了一个不连贯的特例。所以，大概算“新英格兰一带”吧？哦，还有波多黎各和维尔京群岛，距离地球周长只有7%

Moving on to number one, this contains the Keystone Empire plus Delaware. Two spans the North South. Three covers the Deep South. Four stretches the Old Northwest. Five reaches the Highland, six centers the heartland, seven connects the crossroads, eight rises the Mountain West, and nine claims everything else. The West Coast, of course, and Alaska and Hawaii as usual, but also don't forget American Samoa, Guam, and the CMNI,

cues.en: which make Greater Pacifica to mirror Atlantia. So these are the 10 regions told by the first digit of the zip code. Digit two divides again as in the Highlands 5. 59 for Montana, five eight for Dakota, and seven for South. Though with Minnesota, miss much more populous, digit two splits the state in twain. In Iowa, even more, five o, five one, five two. Now you can make a map of America's zip digits one and two that looks like this, but it's not quite right for the actual area the codes cover looks more like this with lots of holes. And, yes, that's a lot of overlap with the federal land map for the same reason. No one lives here. Parks, forest, deserts, no deliveries, no codes needed. Yes. Yes. You've got there. This means zip codes are doing something very different from, say, GPS codes, which can point to any place on Earth exactly,
cues.zh: 它们组成了与亚特兰蒂斯相呼应的“大太平洋区”。这就是由邮编的第一位数字划分出的10个地区。第二位数字会再次进行细分，比如高原地区的5区。59代表蒙大拿，58代表达科他，7代表南达科他。不过由于明尼苏达州人口多得多，第二位数字把该州一分为二。在艾奥瓦州更是如此，有50、51、52。现在你可以画出一张美国邮编第一位和第二位数字的地图，看起来像这样，但它并不完全准确，因为这些编码实际覆盖的区域看起来更像是这样，有很多空白。没错，这与联邦土地地图有很多重叠之处，原因很简单：这里没人住。公园、森林、沙漠，没有投递需求，自然也不需要邮编。没错。没错。你已经明白了。这意味着邮编所做的事情，与比如能精确指向地球上任何地点的GPS坐标有着本质的不同，

cues.en: which is the clue that there's something strange about this map and the real way zip codes work. But let's play pretend again and color the map back in. Still closer inspection shows with the double digits, the map is all melty and pointy with cross border exceptions everywhere.
cues.zh: 这正是这张地图以及美国邮政编码实际工作方式古怪的地方所在。不过我们再假装一下，把地图重新填上颜色。仔细观察双位数区域就会发现，地图到处都是融化的色块和尖角，到处都有跨越边界的特例。

cues.en: So what's happening here? Well, digit three reveals an even stranger map with wild blobs of land that don't make any sense at all because we've been trying to do this all wrong. These three digits don't mark out land. These digits mark out infrastructure.
cues.zh: 这到底是是怎么回事呢？第三位数字揭示了一张更加古怪的地图，上面有完全不合逻辑的奇怪地块，因为我们之前的方法全盘皆错。这三位数字划分的不是土地。这些数字划分的是基础设施。

cues.en: The zip code first three digits point to a specific big building, a sectional facility center. A belted behemoth bundling up all the mail it ingests for who? Not you, but to ship to all the post offices within its area of influence. So that's why this map is all melty because the map isn't really real. Rather, there are sorting centers scattered strategically,
cues.zh: 邮政编码的前三位指向一栋特定的巨型建筑，即分段处理中心。这是一个庞大的分拣巨兽，把接收到的所有邮件打包好准备送给谁？不是送给你，而是运往其辐射范围内的所有邮局。所以这就是为什么这张地图看起来都融化了，因为地图根本不是真实的。相反，这里战略性地分散着各种分拣中心，

cues.en: each numbered and each sorts the mail for the post offices it can reach efficiently. So if you live on the edge of your state, but near another state's sorting center, your zip code follows the sorting code, not the state line. So much simplified, here's what happens when you mail a letter. Digit the first sends it to a zone sorting center, which when it arrives is then sorted by digits the second and third to be sent to the sectional sorter, which when it arrives there is then again sorted by digits the fourth and the fifth to the local post office. And this is where Americans are vaguely aware they're supposed to include four more digits at the end of a zip code, but no one does because America tried to bolt on the plus four code long after her citizens had already learned that the first five alone would get the job done and so didn't bother. With only the most postal perfectionist plus four ing their packages, but as reward, they do get sorted and sent faster because the final code is for the final sort at the final post office onto final truck for the final delivery. And so the greater geographical oddities of the zip code are less odd because zones aren't zones. They're the first step in sorting. A giant fork in the road. Greater Atlanta this way, everything else that way. Then down the road, islands to the left, New England to the right. So the first answer to why this if also this is because the address is where to go, but the postcode is how to get there. The journey, not the destination. And most countries' codes are built the same basic way. Simple human readable directions left
cues.zh: 它们各自拥有编号，并为自己能够高效触达的邮局分拣邮件。因此，如果你住在州的边缘，但靠近另一个州的分拣中心，你的邮政编码遵循的是分拣代码，而不是州界。大大简化之后，当你寄出一封信时，过程如下。第一位数字把它送到区域分拣中心，到达后由第二位和第三位数字进行分拣，以便发送到分段分拣机；到达那里后，再由第四位和第五位数字进行分拣，送往当地邮局。这就是美国人隐约知道他们应该在邮政编码后面再加上四位数字的地方，但根本没人这么做，因为美国在公民们早已习惯仅凭前五位就能搞定寄信这件事之后很久，才勉强推出 plus-four 附加码，所以大家懒得理会。只有最追求完美的邮政偏执狂才会给他们的包裹加上 plus-four，但作为回报，它们确实能更快地被分拣和寄出，因为最后的代码用于最终邮局的最终分拣，装上最终的卡车进行最终的派送。因此，邮政编码中那些更大的地理怪异现象也就不那么奇怪了，因为区域根本不是区域。它们是分拣的第一步。道路上的一个巨大分叉口。大亚特兰大走这边，其他所有地方走那边。然后顺路往前，左边是各个岛屿，右边是新英格兰。所以，对于“为什么这个地方也对应那个地方”的第一个答案是：地址代表要去哪里，而邮政编码代表如何去那里。是旅程，而不是目的地。而且大多数国家的编码都遵循相同的基本构建方式：简单易懂的路线指引，从左

cues.en: characters reveal, more directions to get the letter closer to where it's going, and the address only needed after it's sorted into the truck and the destination within sight. UK probably has the best version of this, adding letters to make sorting centers more memorable. Manchester gets all the m's, Oxford the o's, Yo York, lovely London as capital gets all the compass points. But the rest simplified is the same story. The next digit sorts to a post office and the last to a delivery route. And because the UK code uses letters and is longer than America's, UK codes can sort close enough to almost replace the address entirely. In most cases, you could get away with just the code and the house number and still expect delivery. I mean, I don't live that dangerously, but I'm also the kind of person who writes plus four on my American mail. But looking at this, it's kind of silly. Right? If an old postcode can get this close on its own to replacing the address, if someone started over now, could it be done better? And that's exactly what Ireland thought. Hey, guys. You know we've got GPS codes now. Right? People don't wanna write a long code like that. Yeah. Yeah. But also, the system was written for human sorters centuries ago. We've got giant sorter trons now. Who cares? We don't really need that? Wait. What are you doing? I think I'm gonna start over. How? I'm gonna go random,

cues.en: That's horrifying. But I guess America's America's first digit is basically meaningless as well. But Ireland didn't stop there and went random all the way down, running like mad past every single point in the whole country where mail might be delivered to slap four more characters at complete
cues.zh: 太吓人了。不过我猜美国——美国邮编的首位数字也基本没意义。但爱尔兰没就此打住，而是一路随机到底，像疯了一样跑遍全国每一个可能投递邮件的地点，只为把另外四个字符完全

cues.en: random on the door. And it matters not at all because Ireland created the codes for the giant Swordatrons who can read them and compare them to the big list of all codes in the country where the last four, surprise, are a GPS code in disguise,
cues.zh: 随机地拍在门上。而这根本不重要，因为爱尔兰创建这些编码，是给巨型 Swordatrons 读的，它们能读取编码，并拿来和全国所有编码的大清单比对；结果最后四位——惊喜——其实是伪装的 GPS 编码，

cues.en: which pinpoints the exact place the letter's supposed to land. And since the Sortertrons also know where all the mail trucks go, it's easy peasy for the sorters to sort while still being not too hard for the little humans to remember the little bitty codes to write out their pieces of paper to pass their notes back and forth. And the random postcodes has one more bonus. In other countries, when towns grow or ghost, buildings divide or combine, countries that try to keep their codes in order ish have to move the codes around to maintain that order ish. And the poor humans with houses that haven't changed having to remember now that their new code is just a little different, but not in Ireland for there's no order to maintain at all. If your mailbox never moves, your code never changes. That's the method to the madness. So when Ireland asked herself, why this, if also this, she found a new answer. Make a post code so precise, it becomes the perfect address. So while everywhere else you have to write both the destination and the journey, in Ireland you can write both, probably still should write both, but you don't have to because just the post code alone will do.
cues.zh: 它能精确定位信件该落到哪里。而且既然 Sortertrons 也知道所有邮车会去哪，分拣员分拣起来就小菜一碟；同时又不至于让小小人类太难记住那一小串编码，好写在纸上互相传纸条。随机邮编还有一个好处。在其他国家，当城镇扩张或荒废、建筑拆分或合并时，那些想让编码保持大致顺序的国家，就得把编码搬来搬去，以维持这种大致顺序。而那些房子明明没变的可怜人类，还得记住自己的新编码只是稍微不同——但在爱尔兰不用，因为根本没有什么顺序要维持。只要你的邮箱不挪窝，你的编码就永远不变。这就是疯狂背后的道理。所以，当爱尔兰问自己：如果这样也行，为什么还要那样？她找到了新答案。把邮编做得如此精确，让它成为完美地址。所以别处你得同时写目的地和路线，在爱尔兰你可以两个都写——大概也还是该两个都写——但你不必，因为只写邮编就够了。
这一切看起来都挺复杂的。
